results.title: [K-LIT REVIEW] Life lessons from Min Jin Lee's 'American Hagwon'
results.content: Is "American Hagwon" an engrossing story wrapped in a cultural lesson, or is it the other way around? And does it matter, when the story is this good and when one can learn so much from it? Readers who enjoyed Korean American author Min Jin Lee’s "Pachinko" will be pleased to find some of the same narrative structure applied to her latest story. Yes, it could be called a soap opera, but when a soap opera is great, it holds attention. Focusing on the Koh family, the story spans a generation and three countries. The family oscillates between Korea, the United States and Australia, often living apart as they pursue educational opportunities, job postings and economic security. The parents, Helen and John, are living a familiar life pattern of working as hard as they can to do all they can for their children, Bo, DH and Mido. results.title: Captan Son Heung-min calls difficult year part of growing process
results.content: DOHA — Having wrapped up his ninth year as captain of the men's national football team on Tuesday, Son Heung-min admitted the 2026 has been a particularly challenging one. The Taegeuk Warriors were eliminated in the group stage at the FIFA World Cup in June, when they were expected to not just reach the knockout phase but also win at least one match once there. In the aftermath, Hong Myung-bo, then the team's head coach, and Chung Mong-gyu, president of the Korea Football Association (KFA), both resigned. Then in October, following a friendly victory over Uzbekistan at home, Son found himself in controvery over apparent friction in the locker room. results.title: Lee arrives in Shenzhen for APEC summit
results.content: SHENZHEN, China — South Korean President Lee Jae Myung arrived in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday to attend this week's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. During his stay through Thursday, Lee is scheduled to participate in the APEC CEO summit, a welcoming dinner hosted by Chinese President Xi Jinping and the main summit session, which will be held under the theme, "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together." The APEC summit is expected to coincide with a high-profile meeting among U.S. President Donald Trump, Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin, who are likely to discuss nuclear arms reduction among other international issues. Another major point of attention is whether Trump will meet North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, after the U.S. president repeatedly expressed interest in meeting Kim during his Asian trip. results.title: Nat'l football team ends tumultuous year with narrow win over Qatar
results.content: DOHA — The tumultuous year of 2026 came to an end for the men's national football team with a narrow victory over Qatar on Tuesday in Doha, where the Taegeuk Warriors failed to capitalize on numerous chances. Forward Oh Se-hun's 43rd-minute header was the lone goal in South Korea's 1-0 victory at Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium in the Qatari capital. South Korea peppered Qatar with 22 shot attempts and nine shots on goal, as their attackers took advantage of open space afforded by Qatar's passive defense. Compared to some earlier matches, the South Koreans exhibited more efficient off-the-ball movements and made plays in the attacking third with purpose. However, the two starting forwards, Oh and Son Heung-min, lacked the clinical finishing touch. results.title: S. Korea defeat Qatar in final match of year
results.content: DOHA — South Korea blanked Qatar 1-0 in Doha on Tuesday in their final men's football friendly of the year, prevailing in a match much more lopsided than the final score indicated. Striker Oh Se-hun headed home the match's lone goal late in the first half at Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium in the Qatari capital, where South Korea, ranked 32nd, held 60th-ranked Qatar without a shot in the first half and finished with a 22-2 advantage in shot attempts. Only heroics by the Qatari goalkeeper Salah Zakaria made the final score more respectable This was the sixth and potentially the final match for South Korea's temporary head coach, Robert Moreno. results.title: Lee heads to China for APEC after wrapping up ASEAN summit
results.content: MANILA — South Korean President Lee Jae Myung departed for China on Tuesday to attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, wrapping up his trip to Manila for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit. Lee, who arrived in Manila on Monday, attended the South Korea-ASEAN summit, a gathering with the five Mekong countries — Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand and Vietnam — as well as the ASEAN Plus Three summit involving ASEAN, South Korea, China and Japan. During the meetings, the president stressed the need for closer regional cooperation in responding to complex crises and called for the region's support for his administration's policy of seeking peaceful coexistence on the Korean Peninsula. results.title: 3.6 magnitude earthquake hits city in southeastern S. Korea: weather agency
results.content: A 3.6 magnitude earthquake struck a city in the southeastern province of North Gyeongsang on Tuesday, the weather agency said. The quake hit an area about 22 kilometers northwest of Sangju's city center around 11:10 p.m. with the epicenter located at a depth of 20 km, according to the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA). The agency initially put the magnitude at 3.7 but revised it down to 3.6 after further analysis. It was the strongest of the 58 earthquakes recorded on the Korean Peninsula and in surrounding waters this year. It was also the first quake of magnitude 3.5 or higher in the region in about 18 months, since a magnitude 3.7 tremor struck waters 52 km northwest of Taean in South Chungcheong Province on May 5 last year.
